title: Underdemanded v. Overdemanded
author: Stuart Jr., Dave
summary: Using a Viktor Frankl quote as a launching point, Stuart connects the psychological Yerkes-Dodson law of optimal challenge to a specific claim about the current moment in education: that most students, post-COVID, are underdemanded rather than overdemanded, and that this is the greater risk teachers should be guarding against. He describes the widening range of student preparedness by ninth grade as one of the central practical difficulties of public high school teaching, framing it as a natural consequence of a diverse, unequal society rather than a critique of prior teachers. His central claim is that many of his students are especially hungry for a fair challenge and want to be taken seriously as capable learners, even amid pandemic-era narratives emphasizing trauma and social-emotional accommodation. He closes with a caution against decoupling high expectations from teaching quality, arguing expectations only work when matched by competent instruction, and that teachers must still watch for students who are crushed or bored by demands miscalibrated to them individually.
points: Applies the Yerkes-Dodson Goldilocks Zone of optimal challenge specifically to a post-COVID claim: most students are currently underdemanded, not overdemanded, and that imbalance is the bigger classroom risk right now.
Names widening student preparedness range by ninth grade as a structural feature of an unequal, individualistic society rather than a failure of prior teachers.
Insists high expectations only function when paired with high-quality instruction, rejecting a version of rigor that isn't backed by matched teaching quality.
Frames the challenge of calibrating demand to each student individually, avoiding both crushing and boring them, as core, difficult, paid professional work, not an incidental task.
quotes: Young people should not be overdemanded. However, we have also to consider the fact that at least today, in the age of an affluent society, most people are underdemanded rather than overdemanded.
In human performance, there's a kind of Goldilocks Zone where folks perform best. You and I will see our students grow best when they're neither over- nor under-pressured.

By ninth grade, the range in student preparedness is truly massive. This isn't the "fault" of preceding teachers; it's what's going to happen in a nation as cosmopolitan and individualistic and unequal as ours.
In light of COVID, in light of inequity, in light of social-emotional learning, I do find that many of my students are especially hungry for a fair challenge. They want to be taken seriously.
You can't be a heartless jerk with high expectations. The quality of your teaching has to at least match the level of your expectations.
